subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Tunguska: The Mystery Explosion
description: A fast breakdown of Tunguska: The Mystery Explosion for builders.

hook.text: In 1908, a massive explosion flattened 80 million trees across 2,000 km² of Siberia. No crater was found.

buildup.text: The blast was 1,000 times more powerful than Hiroshima. Windows shattered hundreds of km away.

discovery.text: A small asteroid or comet fragment likely exploded in the atmosphere before ever reaching the ground.

twist.text: Nobody investigated for 19 years because the area was so remote. The forest was already regrowing.

climax.text: If it had arrived 4 hours later, Earth's rotation would have placed St. Petersburg underneath.

punchline.text: No crater, no fragments. Just 80 million flattened trees.

quiz.question: Why was no crater found at the Tunguska explosion site?
options: The object exploded in the atmosphere before hitting the ground
The crater was filled in by volcanic activity shortly after
The explosion occurred over a lake that absorbed the impact

details.summary: On June 30, 1908, a massive explosion over Tunguska, Siberia flattened 2,000 square kilometers of forest — an area the size of a large city. With energy equivalent to 10-15 megatons of TNT, it was likely an asteroid or comet fragment that exploded in the atmosphere.
details.whyItMatters: Tunguska is the largest confirmed asteroid impact event in recorded history. It demonstrates that city-destroying cosmic impacts happen on human timescales — the Tunguska event occurred only 116 years ago over a fortunately remote area.
takeaways: A 1908 explosion over Siberia flattened 2,000 sq km of forest
It released energy equal to 10-15 megatons of TNT
No crater or fragments were found — it exploded in the atmosphere

faq.question: What caused the Tunguska explosion?
faq.answer: Most likely a rocky asteroid 50-80 meters in diameter that entered the atmosphere at high speed and exploded at an altitude of 5-10 kilometers. The explosion was an airburst — the object disintegrated completely without reaching the ground, explaining the absence of a crater and meteorite fragments.

faq.question: What if Tunguska happened over a city today?
faq.answer: A Tunguska-scale event over a major city would cause catastrophic destruction — potentially millions of casualties and hundreds of billions of dollars in damage. The explosion was 1,000 times more powerful than the Hiroshima bomb. Such events occur roughly every 500-1,000 years on average.
